subject: Post-demo: Success lexicon + performance sprint plan
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel@latticeworks.io>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@latticeworks.io>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up — quick notes

Thanks for the demo today — appreciate the concise walkthrough. A few things I want captured so our internal folks can align:

- Primary objective: Replace our current summarization pipeline with a low-latency Redwood-backed endpoint for agent assist.
- Traffic profile: 60k unique users/month, ~1.2M inference calls/month, median request payload ~220 tokens, peak concurrent ~45 rps.
- Risk areas: hallucination on billing/legal prompts, throughput during morning spikes, and integration with our Kafka-based ingest.

Can you put together a short success rubric (latency/throughput/cost/quality) and a proposed sprint plan for the PoC? We'll need this to brief procurement and platform engineering by next Tuesday.

—Daniel
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@latticeworks.io>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up — quick notes

Thanks Daniel — summary below and an ask for alignment. Attaching a short M.A.P. and sample workload for your infra team.

TL;DR (proposed PoC scope)
- Duration: 6 weeks (2-week sandbox + 3-week integration + 1-week validation)
- Success metrics: p95 latency, steady-state throughput, cost/token target, and quality thresholds tied to a canonical prompt set
- Redwood owners: kimberly_park (sales lead), ben_carter (CS/ops lead), mina_haddad (runtime eng lead)
- Customer owners: Daniel Park (CTO), Priya Shah (Platform Eng)

Requested next steps:
1) Confirm sandbox start date (we recommend Oct 26)
2) Share service account details and sample Kafka topics for ingest access
3) Procurement: indicate preferred PO cadence so we can prepare SOW language

I'll follow up with a detailed rubric and sprint calendar in a separate message.

Best,
Kimberly
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@latticeworks.io>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 09:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up — PoC operational assumptions

Looping in ops/eng assumptions so Priya can validate:

Operational assumptions
- Expected steady-state throughput for the PoC: 35 rps (conservative), target peak bursts up to 60 rps for short windows.
- Typical sequence length: median 220 tokens; worst-case 1024 tokens for archival queries.
- KV cache: enabled for repeated context to reduce token cost; we will instrument cache hit rate during sandbox.
- Deployment: single-region US-West for latency testing; can add EU region for DR in later stages.

Attachment: sample-workload.json (contains 200 representative queries derived from your demo)

Ben — can you confirm the SLOs below are achievable with minimal infra changes?
From: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Daniel Park <daniel@latticeworks.io>
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PoC rubric + performance targets

Thanks — quick pass from engineering. Proposed measurable success lexicon (we'll validate these during sandbox):

Performance
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 180 ms for request size <= 256 tokens; p95 <= 450 ms for requests up to 1024 tokens.
- Throughput: steady-state >= 40 rps with 99% request success (no 5xx) on the configured benchmark workload; tolerate short bursts to 70 rps for <= 60s.
- Availability: endpoint availability >= 99.9% during validation window.

Cost
- Target cost: <= $0.0009 per token (average across workload) with recommended int8 quantization and batching; provide a cost breakdown after sandbox runs.

Quality
- Canonical prompt pass-rate: >= 91% (measured vs. customer-provided gold answers on a 150-example validation set).
- Hallucination rate: < 2% (false assertions on safety/legal prompts).
- Semantic similarity: mean embedding cosine >= 0.78 on paraphrase checks (automated proxy).

Data and instrumentation
- We will instrument per-request latency, token usage, KV cache hit rate, and a per-prompt quality flag. Logs/metrics will be shared to your Grafana/Datadog project via our read-only integration.

Ownership and gating
- Sandbox (week 1-2): engineering validation of endpoints, run initial cost profile. Owner: mina_haddad (R).
- Integration (week 3-5): connect Kafka, run live traffic slice, confirm throughput. Owner: Priya Shah (customer) + ben_carter (ops).
- Validation (week 6): run full 150-example golden set, produce pass/fail report. Decision gate: pass-rate and cost targets.

We'll also include a fall-back plan (lower-capacity variant, longer tail latency SLO) if cost spikes.

-Mina
Senior Runtime Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Daniel Park <daniel@latticeworks.io>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PoC rubric + performance targets

This is great — thank you for the clear, measurable targets. Quick responses to close the loop: 

- Sandbox start: we can confirm Oct 28 (our infra team needs two days to share service account).
- Priya will lead integration; I added her to this thread.
- Procurement: we aim to get a PO approved by Nov 11; please include a one-page SOW with milestone-based billing.

Two small asks before kickoff:
1) Can Redwood include a short regression checklist for hallucination checks we can run internally?
2) Can you provide an expected cost-sensitivity table showing cost/token vs. batch size and KV hit rate?

If those two items are in the mutual action plan, we'll be aligned. Looking forward to the sandbox.

—Daniel
